content.text:
I built step 1 of the habit tracker as three files: `index.html`, `style.css` and `app.js`. I checked that the script has no syntax errors and that the week dates come out right, but I haven't opened the page in a browser. Open `index.html` to try it; there's no build step and nothing to install.

**What it does:**
- **Add habits:** type a name and press Enter or click Add.
- **Tick off days:** each habit has a checkbox for every day of the current week, Monday to Sunday. Today's column is highlighted, and each row shows how many days are done (e.g. `3/7`).
- **Delete habits:** the ✕ button removes a habit, after asking you to confirm.
- **Saving:** everything is stored in `localStorage` under the key `habitTracker.v1`. Each habit stores the dates it was ticked (e.g. `"2026-11-22": true`), so past weeks are kept even though only the current week is shown.

**Other details:**
- Dates use your local time, so a tick late in the evening isn't recorded on the wrong day.
- If the page stays open past midnight, it moves on to the new day or week by itself.
- If you have it open in two tabs, changes in one show up in the other.
- If the saved data is damaged, the page starts with an empty list instead of crashing.

I tested the week calculation on a Sunday, a Monday, and a week that crosses into the next year; all came out correct. I only did step 1 and haven't read `STEP-2.md` or `STEP-3.md`.

content.text:
I added both features: each habit now has a streak counter, and there's a weekly completion percentage per habit and for the week as a whole. I tested the code in Node with a small stand-in for the browser page, using preset data and a fixed "today" (Sunday 22 Nov). I haven't opened it in a real browser.

**Streak (new column)**
- Shows how many days in a row a habit has been ticked, counting back from today, e.g. `🔥 5`. It can go back past the start of this week.
- If today isn't ticked yet, the streak still counts up to yesterday and shows a small "tick today" note. It only resets once a whole day is missed.
- Ticking days later in the week doesn't add to the streak.

**Weekly percentage**
- **Per habit:** the Week column shows `5/7` with `71%` under it.
- **Whole week:** a summary panel above the table shows the overall percentage with a progress bar. Under it is a line like "10 of 21 check-ins done · Longest current streak: Read (5 days)". The panel is hidden when there are no habits.
- The percentage is out of all 7 days, so on a Wednesday 100% isn't possible yet. Basing it on "days so far" instead would be a one-line change if you prefer that.
- Ticking a box updates that habit's numbers and the summary straight away.

**What the test showed:**
- A 5-day run that started last week gave a streak of 5.
- A habit not ticked today showed 3 with the "tick today" note, and ticking today raised it to 4.
- Unticking a day in the middle cut Read's streak from 5 to 3, and the summary then named Run as the longest streak.
- The overall figure went 48% → 52% → 48% as boxes changed.
- After deleting every habit, the summary and table were hidden.

**Cleanup needed:** my request to delete the temporary test folder `.tmp-test\` wasn't approved, so it's still in the project. It only holds the test script `run.js`, which the app doesn't use. You can delete it, or approve the deletion and I'll remove it.

The changes are in `index.html`, `style.css` and `app.js`. Saved data from step 1 still loads; nothing about how it's stored changed.

content.text:
I added a dark mode toggle that remembers your choice, and cleaned up the code across all three files. I tested it in Node with a stand-in for the browser page, and all checks passed. I still haven't opened it in a real browser, so the dark colours haven't been checked by eye.

**Dark mode**
- A **🌙 Dark / ☀️ Light** button sits at the top right and always offers the other mode.
- Your choice is saved in `localStorage` under `habitTracker.theme`, so it's still set on the next visit.
- Until you click it, the page follows your system's light/dark setting, including if that setting changes while the page is open. Once you choose, your choice wins.
- A short script in `<head>` applies the theme before the page draws, so it doesn't flash light first.
- Changing the theme in one tab updates other open tabs.
- I checked the text and background colour contrast in both themes. Everything meets the usual 4.5:1 accessibility guideline.

**Tidy-up**
- **`app.js`:**
  - Repeated code now lives in shared helpers: finding a row's habit, the new-day check, and the "day/days" wording.
  - Today's date and the week's dates are worked out once per render. Before, the streak code read the clock separately, so just after midnight streaks and the table could disagree.
  - Every element is now built the same way, with no `innerHTML` strings.
  - "7" is a named constant, and the code is grouped into sections.
- **`style.css`:**
  - Reorganised into sections, with all colours set as theme variables. Nothing is hard-coded any more.
  - Renamed `--accent-dark` to `--accent-text`, since the old name was wrong in dark mode.
  - The text box and buttons now take their font and colours from the theme, so they look right in dark mode.
  - Added one keyboard-focus outline style for the whole page.
  - Two duplicate rules were merged.
- **Contrast fixes in both themes:** white text on the Add button was below the 4.5:1 guideline and is now about 5:1. The grey text was slightly too light on the summary panel and is now darker.
- **Screen reader:** ticking a box used to make it read out the whole summary panel. Now it only reads the one changed line, e.g. "11 of 21 check-ins done".

**What the test checked**
- The step 2 streak and percentage results are unchanged, and adding, ticking and deleting habits still save correctly.
- The theme follows the system setting when nothing is saved.
- A saved choice wins over the system setting, both on load and when the setting changes later.
- An invalid saved value falls back to the system setting.
- A theme change in another tab is picked up.

I deleted the `.tmp-test\` folder, so the project now holds only `index.html`, `style.css`, `app.js` and the three task files. That's all three steps done.
